fact: Median mise run: 37.5 subagent spawns, 818k output tokens, 5.38 active hours, 26.1 wall hours, 13 owner turns (n=28 runs).
source: runs/run-costs.md §Run index + runs/run-costs.jsonl (medians computed here over the 28 rows)
caveat: 6 of 42 sessions lost their raw transcript; 10.1% of active time is booked to (unattributed).

fact: Share of all generated output tokens by role: implementer 31.0%, driver 23.9%, other 9.9%, critic 9.4%, reviewer 9.1%, fix 7.9%, documenter 4.9%, acceptance 3.1%, retrospective 0.8%.
caveat: Subagent duration sums overlap (parallel agents); shares are of output tokens, which are ~1/100 of input+cache.

fact: Share of active time by stage: execute 66.1%, (unattributed) 10.1%, plan 8.6%, acceptance 6.6%, requirements 4.0%, goals 2.9%, setup 0.7%, mock 0.5%, retrospective 0.4%.
caveat: Permission-prompt wait is charged to toolMs, so active time is an upper bound.

fact: Per task in execute: median 4.0 subagent spawns, 65k output tokens, 44 active minutes (p90 7.4 / 189k / 87).
caveat: Only runs with a task count, an execute stage and a complete raw transcript.

fact: The driver (main thread) is 23.9% of output and 35.1% of input over 11,808 requests; it re-reads interaction.md 1.50x/run, execute.md 1.21x, goals.md 0.93x, plan.md 0.86x.
caveat: Skill-body injections (144, 287k est. tokens) are counted separately from file reads.

fact: Human-wait totals 1213.9 h against 387.3 h of active model+tool time (3.1:1); 141.9 h capped at 30 min/gap. Acceptance holds 34.7% of all wait at 16.5:1 wait:active; execute 39.7% at 1.9:1.
caveat: Wait is a lower bound because permission-prompt time sits inside toolMs.

fact: Small runs (<=400 changed code lines, n=7): median 11 subagents, 228k output tokens, 1.62 active h, 14.9 wall h, 458 mise artifact lines, 2.3x artifact:code, 8 owner turns. Runs >400 lines (n=21): 68 subagents, 1.44M tokens, 13.7 active h, 0.31x artifact:code.
caveat: Only 1 of the 7 is at or under 60 changed lines.

fact: Okven runs of 60 or fewer changed lines carried 354-662 artifact lines: ratios 14.6x to 59.4x artifact lines per code line (n=6, 4 with artifacts recoverable).
caveat: Per-stage elapsed exists for only 2 of the 6; the rest reached git in one sync.

fact: Elapsed hours rise with size: 0-60 LOC median 2.0 h (n=2 usable), 501-2000 21.7 h, 2001-10000 163.4 h, >10000 189.9 h.
scope: okven, n=34 runs, 14 with usable timelines
caveat: Elapsed is commit-timestamp span, not time worked; 20 of 34 runs have no usable timeline.

fact: critic-requirements: 74 subagent runs, 125.8M tokens, 8.6 agent-hours, 711 findings, 216 defect/convention findings that changed something, 582k tokens per such change.
caveat: Outcome is inferred from token overlap with the next dispatch; script-vs-hand agreement on substance is 52%.

fact: critic-plan: 90 runs, 430.0M tokens, 15.3 agent-hours, 820 findings, 248 defect/convention changes, 1.73M tokens per change.
caveat: Same outcome-inference caveat; 15% of critic-plan extracted rows are extraction artifacts.

fact: Critic rounds 1-2 buy changes ~3x cheaper than rounds 3+: requirements r1+r2 = 25 runs / 30.7M tokens / 104 changes (295k each) vs r3+ = 49 runs / 95.1M / 112 changes (850k each); plan r1+r2 = 38 runs / 134.8M / 112 changes (1.20M each) vs r3+ = 52 runs / 295.3M / 136 changes (2.17M each).
caveat: The r3-5 bucket cannot be split, so a cap of exactly 3 is interpolated from r1/r2/r6+ trends.

fact: Critic rounds 6+ cost 197.3M tokens over 48 runs for 61 changes: 3.2M tokens per change, 5.5x the round-1 rate.
caveat: Round is scoped to branch+target; two branches that ran mise twice merge both loops.

fact: Critic gates rarely settle in one round: requirements mean 5.7 rounds (max 14), 8% settle in one; plan mean 4.5 (max 25), 10% settle in one.
caveat: Targets, not runs; a branch that ran mise twice inflates its round depth.

fact: Of 60 (run, gate) pairs with a recorded round count, 38 settle at 3 rounds or fewer with 6 stalls; the 22 that go to 4+ rounds contain 17 of the 23 stalls. Rounds >=5 is 16 pairs, 12 stalled.
source: runs/friction.md §Gate rounds per gate per run
caveat: Counts exist only where .mise/_friction.md survived; a gate can report several stall counts, so max-per-gate is used.

fact: The critic gates are the largest self-reported friction source: 100 requirements items + 95 plan items across 30 and 34 runs, top category 'slow'. The single most repeated friction cluster is 'critic requirements: stalled' (27 items, 11 runs, 6 repos).
source: runs/friction.md §Items by implicated mechanism + §20 most repeated
caveat: Friction lines are written by the run itself; 674 of 1598 items are category 'other' and unanalysed.

fact: The owner broke critic stalls by hand twice inside one run ('user approved requirements after the stall without a further critic round', same for the plan) and asked in chat 'we should reset the critic count' and 'are we better off if we just start from the mocks again?'.
caveat: Two runs; verbatim but not a rate.

fact: Per-task reviewer: 236 runs, 501.3M tokens, 31.3 agent-hours, 382 findings, 270 changed something (71% - the highest change rate of any gate), 173 defect/convention changes at 2.9M tokens each; 98% of targets settle in one round.
caveat: 30% of reviewer extracted rows are extraction artifacts; the substance split is indicative.

fact: 53% of reviewer targets (123 of 231) produced no defect or convention finding in any round, costing 232.7M tokens.
caveat: 'No finding' includes findings the splitter classified 'unclear' (32% of reviewer findings).

fact: 6 of the 10 hand-verified most valuable catches in the corpus are reviewer round 1; 2 are critic-plan, 1 critic-requirements, 1 reviewer. Each was read in full before being called a catch.
scope: n=10, drawn from 57 hand-classified changed findings
caveat: Selection is hand-ranked by severity and outcome strength, not a random sample.

fact: Acceptance pass: 94 runs, 324.0M tokens, 9.8 agent-hours, 425 findings, only 42 defect/convention findings changed anything - 7.7M tokens per change, the worst ratio of any gate. 55% of its findings drew no visible response. Mean 4.5 rounds, max 20; 45 of 94 runs are round 6+.
caveat: no-visible-response is an upper bound on 'ignored'; the driver usually rejects silently.

fact: Acceptance round 1 = 21 runs / 83.0M tokens / 11 defect-or-convention changes; rounds 2+ = 73 runs / 241.0M tokens / 31 changes. Rounds 2+ are 74% of acceptance token spend.
caveat: Same round-scoping caveat as E-013.

fact: End-of-plan gate (delegated e2e/sanity runs): 94 runs, 353.2M tokens, 27.6 agent-hours, 6 findings total, 0 of them changed anything. 12 of 13 targets never produced a defect or convention finding; mean 7.2 rounds, max 20.
caveat: Only the delegated part is counted; main-thread Format/Check/unit-test failures are not in this number.

fact: End-of-plan gate rounds 2+: 81 runs, 343.0M tokens, 1 finding. 8 of the 10 most wasteful individual gate rounds in the corpus are end-of-plan gate runs at 14.9-21.5M tokens each with 0 findings.
caveat: Wasteful is defined as 'no defect-or-convention finding that changed anything', which understates a gate that legitimately passed.

fact: The gate's own restart clause is a named failure: stages/execute.md re-runs the gate from step 1 after any commit past a finished gate, and provenance records that this is how eric/attribution-3's documenter churn happened (the step-1 documenter was removed for it, 133d2de).
source: inventory/provenance.md §Added in response to a named real failure
caveat: One run; the clause itself (re-run from step 1) was not removed, only its first step.

fact: Documenter: 139 gate runs, 314.0M tokens, 15.7 agent-hours, 0 findings by design; 166 spawns (8.6% of all), 2.36M output (4.9%); mean 1.5 rounds, max 11. In mise 2.1.0 it grew to 10.0% of output.
caveat: The documenter is a producer, not a checker, so 0 findings is expected; the cost columns are the whole measurement.

fact: Documenter-stage commits run an 11.66 comment:code ratio (2,437 comment lines vs 209 code lines) plus 7,272 markdown lines; implementer-stage commits run 0.22. Repo-wide the ratio is 0.31.
caveat: Historical comment detection is regex-based, not AST-based; a template-literal line starting with // counts as a comment.

fact: One documenter commit rewrote comments across 61 files in a single pass: fix/menu-pin 45b0bad8c, 349 insertions / 100 deletions, of which 345 added and 100 removed are comment lines. Provenance names it as the trigger for 2.1.0's documenter-scope narrowing.
source: inventory/provenance.md §Added in response to a named real failure (133d2de)
caveat: One commit; the narrowing shipped, so the current documenter is narrower than the one measured.

fact: docs/design/attribution.md was rewritten 95 times to land at 241 lines.
caveat: Squash merges hide authored dates; the count is of commits touching the file across refs.

fact: mise 2.1.0 exists to fix 'the token and wall-clock regression 2.0.0 introduced, measured on two okven runs'. 2.0.0 is the release that added the documenter role, the project checklist and the end-of-plan gate.
caveat: The regression measurement itself is the commit message's claim; the two runs are not named in the repo.

fact: Retrospective: 17 runs, 36.2M tokens, 1.9 agent-hours, 159 numbered proposals. Adoption at target-file HEAD: 24 adopted + 29 likely-adopted (33%), 40 partly, 55 not-found, 11 undetermined.
caveat: 'adopted' is a git log -S text match; a reworded adoption reads as not-found.

fact: 0 of 46 plugin-candidate proposals were ever found in the mise repo's history. The one .mise/_upstream-feedback.md ever written (9 proposals, hand-checked) scored 1 adopted, 3 partly, 5 not adopted.
scope: 1 run (okven eric/attribution, mise 1.6.0) plus 46 transcript-parsed proposals
caveat: Hand-check covers 9 proposals from one run; the 46 use an automated rare-token signal only.

fact: Retrospective proposals never repeat across runs: 159 rare-token clusters at Jaccard >=0.45, 0 spanning 2 or more runs; at >=0.25, 1 cluster spans 2 runs and 0 span 3+.
caveat: Rare-token Jaccard is a lexical proxy; two proposals with the same intent and different wording do not cluster.

fact: Rules written from the owner's corrections do land: 22 of 41 rule-escape downgrades are rules committed within hours of the burst of notes they answer, across three separate occasions (CLAUDE.md:87, functions/CLAUDE.md:21, CLAUDE.md:84).
scope: okven, n=41 downgrades of 178 claimed escapes
caveat: Dating is by git log -S of the rule phrase; an earlier differently-worded version would be missed.

fact: Writing the rule down and making a role answer for it did not stop the defect: okven's doc-style 'prose rule 10' and 'prose rule 15' both existed, were answered pass by the checklist-answering roles, and the owner still flagged them at the acceptance gate on three separate runs.
caveat: Three runs; the friction lines are the run's own self-report of what the owner flagged.

fact: Every checklist rule is answered three or more times: okven's checklist sits at 14 of the 15-rule cap, all 14 answered by the implementer, again by every fix implementer, and independently again by the reviewer (mise 2.0.0).
caveat: Reported in the commit that changed it; the reviewer's re-answer was narrowed to verification in 2.1.0.

fact: Checklist answers were 46% dead weight in the progress log: eric/attribution-3's _progress.md reached 56,330 words over 68 entries, 26,172 of them the '- Checklist:' bullets.
caveat: One run, the largest in the corpus; 2.1.0 moved the answers to commit bodies.

fact: Progress logs today: median 104 lines per run, max 6,398; checklist-answer lines median 8 per run.
caveat: Line counts are of the last version surviving in git before the run deleted the directory.

fact: Escape corpus: 537 distinct Delta Review notes over 16 mise runs, 4 repos, 2026-07-27..09-19. 137 (25.5%) are verified rule escapes - a written project rule existed at note time and was broken. Every one of the 537 is by construction a defect that passed mise's critic, reviewer and acceptance gates.
caveat: 421 of 955 responded note ids have no surviving text, so the record is biased toward branches where the owner used Clear Resolved.

fact: Escape categories: test-style 127, convention-violation 71, question 69, wrong-behaviour 64, naming 50, ui-visual 45, dead-or-duplicate 37, comment-doc-slop 35, over-engineering 25, missed-requirement 8.
caveat: Blind re-classification of every 4th note agreed 95.5%; all 6 disagreements were on the question boundary.

fact: A rule already existed for: 45% of naming notes (24/53), 46% of dead-or-duplicate (16/35), 43% of test-style (50/115), 38% of convention-violation (26/69), 33% of comment-doc-slop (11/33) - but 0% of ui-visual (0/44), 2% of wrong-behaviour (1/59), 0% of over-engineering (0/21).
caveat: 'A rule existed' uses the corrected rule dating from escapes.md §0.2.

fact: 62 of 162 test-style and comment/doc notes had no written rule at note time at all; another 12 were covered by a rule that does not actually cover them.
caveat: Coverage is complete and disjoint and self-checked by tools/taxonomy.py, but the sub-pattern assignment is hand judgement.

fact: The test-style escapes are lintable and were measured: a read-only ESLint probe over okven's 756 test files returned 2,649 hits across 300 files - drilling inside expect() 1,467 (T1a), mock.calls indexing 974 (T1b), undefined-snapshot 119 (T1c), vi.mock misplacement 70 (T7). toThrow and toMatchSnapshot return 0 hits: the owner catches every one by hand.
scope: okven at HEAD, 756 test files, ESLint 10.7
caveat: Hit counts are not defect counts - legitimate reads such as expect(wrapper.vm.x) sit inside the 542 T1a field reads; the rule needs an allow-list or a ratchet before it can be an error.

fact: The comment/doc escapes are only partly lintable: D1 (colon/semicolon/em-dash register) and D4 (length caps) need a ~20-line local rule over sourceCode.getAllComments(), which okven can host because it already ships local flat-config rules; D2 (coined jargon), D3 (stale comment), D5 (missing why) and D6 (history-log doc) have no lint expression at all.
caveat: The D1/D4/D7 selectors were written but NOT run; only the 10 test-style selectors were executed.

fact: No lint rule anywhere in okven enforces the test-style family. The only test-style rule with lint backing is 'no describe()'. The rest of eslint.config.mjs restricts comment position, comment length, ID casts, handle* delegation and attribution imports.
caveat: Read at HEAD on 2026-09-19; a rule added since is not reflected.

fact: mise's own gates caught 104 defects (per-task reviewer friction lines) against 594 the owner caught himself (57 acceptance-gate flags plus 537 Delta Review notes).
caveat: Units differ - a task finding can bundle several defects, a Delta note is one - so this is an order of magnitude, not a ratio.

fact: Owner turns in mise runs: 1,092 across 43 of 43 mise-invoked sessions. Approval 270, redirect 251, answer 222, correction 190, unrelated 105, process-complaint 54.
caveat: An independent every-28th-row re-check agreed only 79%; approval and redirect should be read as one bucket of 521.

fact: 350 of 1,092 owner turns (32%) are spent in the goals stage before any code exists; requirements 201, plan 164, execute 141, close-out 38, no stage 189.
caveat: miseStage is null on 189 rows (17%).

fact: Only 4 of the 222 questions mise asked the owner were answerable from the repo. 212 (95.5%) are product, design or business decisions only the owner holds.
caveat: answerWasInRepo is a bounded judgement - the classifier read okven's CLAUDE.md files, mise config, checklist, spanish-voice and doc-style, not every product doc in every repo.

fact: The numbered/lettered question format is measurably used: 52 of 222 answers are 3 characters or fewer ('1a', '2b'), 76 are 10 or fewer, median 51; 165 of 270 approvals are 10 characters or fewer, median 8.
caveat: Class labels for approval vs redirect are unstable (79% independent agreement).

fact: 54 verbatim process complaints: 19 are 'output too long or unreadable', 8 'mise proceeds without showing the change or without approval', 8 'work the owner did not want or run in the wrong place', 4 'a question or its answer got lost', 4 'mise's own rule not followed', 3 'a gate runs before I finish reviewing', 3 'the critic loop is not converging', 3 artifact bloat, 2 pacing.
caveat: Recall is deliberately generous and still a floor; 30 of the 54 are low confidence.

fact: The single largest owner-correction type is not a code defect: 67 of 190 corrections (35%) are the owner iterating on a mock or a rendered layout, 44 of them in the goals stage and 19 in okven's plan stage.
caveat: Type was hand-assigned from the verbatim clause; a keyword pass misfired on 9 of 30 and was discarded.

fact: Only 8 of 190 in-chat corrections are test defects and 6 are comment/doc slop - those two classes are caught in Delta Review after the run, not in chat during it.
caveat: Proximity-based role attribution; lastMiseRole is null on 419 of 1092 rows.

fact: Note-to-fix latency: median 31.9 minutes, p90 144.5 minutes (n=270 notes whose fix commit the agent cited). Only 4.4% of those fixes landed inside a /mise:next run; 55.2% were an ad hoc chat turn with no skill or slash command in the window.
caveat: Uses the sha the agent named in its own response; notes fixed without a cited sha are invisible.

fact: 41.7% of sampled agent responses to a review note produced no code change of any kind; 15% are explicit pushback where the agent argued the code was right.
scope: n=60 responses read, 12 re-read blind with 12/12 agreement
caveat: 60 of 534 responses; corpus-wide regex lower bound is 10.5% explicit no-change.

fact: The shipped plugin is 743 non-blank prose lines across skills/next/** (SKILL.md 91, plan.md 102, execute.md 90, interaction.md 79, goals.md 48, setup.md 41, requirements.md 27, six role files 228, config-reference 64), plus 206 lines of repo docs and 601 lines of state.ts.
source: inventory/mise-flow.md §1, inventory/mise-roles.md §1, and scorecard/mechanism-map.jsonl (distinct lines computed here)
caveat: Rows overlap where one line carries several rules, so kind totals exceed line totals.

fact: 34 instructions are restated across 2 to 10 separate locations in the driver files; 93 direct cross-role duplication links exist among the role files, and 52 of the 186 behavioural role rows restate something 2 or more other roles are also told.
caveat: overlapsWith is the inventory agent's reading of shared subject matter; the files carry no marker, so the 93 is a judgement.

fact: 37 of the 44 state.ts invariants are restated in prose, 16 of those restating lines sitting in runtime-loaded files. docs/state-machine.md (53 non-blank lines, 33 inventory rows) is never read at runtime by the skill - only state.ts:7 and README.md reference it.
caveat: The restatement search was grep-driven; a restatement in different vocabulary could have been missed.

fact: references/interaction.md:7 states there are exactly two human gates. The line-level inventory finds 30 distinct human-stop sites, 11 of them terminal.
caveat: Stop sites are counted from the instruction text, not from how often each actually fired.

fact: Worst case spawns for a run of T tasks is 7T + 19 + N + 4F in two-pass mode (4T + 19 + N + 3F single pass). The explore count N, the user-flagged acceptance rounds F, and the goals/mock gate loop have no stated bound anywhere in the text.
caveat: Structural reading of the instruction files, not an observed count.

fact: Explore subagents are barely used: 35 plan-stage non-critic spawns across 28 runs, median 0 per run, max 6. The _exploration_notes.md they feed is median 64 lines, max 624.
caveat: Role resolution puts explore inside 'other'; the count is of plan-stage non-critic spawns, a proxy.

fact: Provenance trigger mix over 89 mechanism rows: named-failure-in-a-real-run 24, owner-preference 23, unknown 19, refactor 13, speculative 10. Eight rows have no stated reason anywhere.
caveat: No .mise/ artifacts survive for 1.0.0-1.5.0, which is why 19 rows are unknown.

fact: The two most-reworked mechanisms in the plugin's history are the setup interview and the critic gate, 6 commits each; 11 mechanisms were reworked 3 or more times.
caveat: laterChurn lists were curated, not machine-derived; the independent section-level count is main-line only.

fact: Config drift: okven overrides 13 of 24 knobs (including all 7 Models lines, a checklist at the 15-rule cap with 821 words and only 3 of 15 in the mandated shape, and prose in the Format slot) and adds 3 sections the reference defines nowhere. This repo overrides 4 and omits Task tests entirely.
caveat: Only the current working-tree configs were read; earlier overrides were not examined.

fact: Guide reach is uneven: the doc-style skill body reaches the documenter in 111 of 115 runs, the reviewer in 14 of 111, acceptance 1 of 15, and the critic 0 of 50. The checklist reaches the critic in 2 of 50 runs. The config entry LINE reaches every role (865 subagent transcripts contain it).
caveat: Per-role percentages mix all branches and dates; runs where a role had no reason to read a file are not separated out.

fact: Quality-gate commands (test/lint/typecheck/build) are 7,478 strict runs and 73.5 hours - 19.0% of all active time. 195 of the 467 repeated commands (41.8%) had no file edit in the same thread in between.
caveat: Commands are matched on a 200-character prefix, so two long commands sharing a prefix count as one.

fact: Session transcripts expire: 177 subagent transcripts and 6 whole sessions were deleted by 30-day retention between the 2026-09-19 digest run and the 2026-09-20 12:35Z snapshot, including whole runs (feat/migrate-firebase-kit, feat/backfill-order-history).
caveat: The corpus shrinks daily; re-running the scripts later will not reproduce these numbers.

fact: Setup has the worst wait-to-active ratio of any stage (12.0:1, 32.4 h wait against 2.7 h active over 28 runs) and the mock stage the second worst (16.0:1, 29.3 h against 1.8 h).
caveat: Wait excludes nothing; overnight gaps are in the uncapped figure.

fact: Requirements and its critic earn nothing on small and medium work: critic-requirements on 61-2000 LOC runs = 2 runs, 2 findings, 0 changed; on >2000 LOC runs = 53 runs, 554 findings, 173 changes. Reviewer on <=60 LOC = 1 run, 0 findings; acceptance on <=60 LOC = 2 runs, 0 defect/convention changes.
scope: okven branches joined by code LOC, n=907 role-resolved runs
caveat: Only okven runs could be joined to a size; the small and medium buckets have 1-9 runs each.

fact: The colocated-test rule causes the defect it is meant to prevent: 3 notes are the inverse of the rule (the agent added tests the project convention forbids), and mise's own friction records 'user removed the restored Checkbox.test.ts - no other atom has a colocated test, so the gate repair applied the new-file rule where the surrounding convention is none'.
caveat: Four incidents; the rule is okven's own config value, not a plugin default.

fact: Okven-wide, the named defect 'tests not using inline snapshots' is literally absent: 5,357 toMatchInlineSnapshot, 0 toMatchSnapshot, 0 .snap files ever across 8,822 refs. The one .snap file the owner caught (R216) appears in no commit and no review ref - which is what a defect the owner always catches looks like in git.
caveat: Survivorship: git cannot see this defect class precisely because the owner catches it before it commits.

fact: Two-pass mode is on in okven (Models: documenter: fable) and off in this repo, and the documenter role ran on fable in 105 of its 139 gate runs.
caveat: Model attribution mixes two vocabularies; 36 of 168 records in the largest session resolve to unknown.

fact: Resumability is load-bearing: 42 sessions across 28 runs, median 26.1 wall hours against 5.38 active, 46 recorded compactions with a maximum of 12 in one run, and a 3.1:1 wait-to-active ratio.
caveat: 6 runs' sessions were pruned, so the session count is a floor.

fact: The baseline gate fired 4 times across 4 runs (all tool-or-env), the implementer reported blocked/stuck 3 times across 3 runs, and the documenter 2 times across 2 runs.
scope: 10 repos, 51 runs with a friction log
caveat: Counted from friction-line prefixes; a firing the run did not log is invisible.

fact: Stage cost shifted sharply between 2.0.0 (n=21) and 2.1.0 (n=7): execute went 59.6% -> 77.4% of output and plan 12.1% -> 4.7%, goals 7.5% -> 1.3%; documenter went 3.0% -> 10.0% of output and reviewer 7.5% -> 13.2%.
caveat: The version ceiling is when a version landed on main, not when the owner installed it; n=7 for 2.1.0.

fact: Fix dispatches are 154 spawns (8.0%), 3.83M output (7.9%) and 12.3% of all execute-stage output - the channel through which the reviewer's 270 changed findings actually land.
caveat: The 'fix' role is a dispatch shape of the implementer, not a separate role file.

fact: Per-task review found defects in 224 friction lines across 36 runs, median 3.5 per run, max 46; acceptance user-flags 70 lines across 21 runs, median 2, max 12.
scope: 10 repos, 51 runs with a friction log
caveat: Line counts, not defect counts; a line can bundle several defects.

fact: The mock stage is entered in 10 of 28 runs and costs 4 spawns, 0.8% of output and 1.8 active hours in total; median mock artifact lines across all 28 runs is 0.
caveat: One originhypnosis run that never left goals distorts the adjacent goals row (44 parallel design agents).

fact: Small runs' stage medians (n=7, <=400 LOC): setup 0.9 active min / 2.0k output, goals 7.5 / 21.9k, requirements 3.4 / 15.4k, plan 18.2 / 54.2k, execute 37.3 / 102.2k, acceptance 6.3 / 17.5k, retrospective 0.9 / 12.4k.
caveat: Stage medians do not sum to the run median; 2 of the 7 have a pruned session.

fact: The plugin's CLAUDE.md ship guard has a named origin: a version bump that never reached an installed user, because Claude Code installs and updates by version and no test or quality gate catches a missing bump (cb905af, 2026-08-14).
source: inventory/provenance.md §Added in response to a named real failure
caveat: One incident, recorded in the commit message itself.

fact: The branch question was reworked from a real owner correction recorded in the run itself: '.mise/_friction.md: correction: review notes on v2 files - branch question skipped for a new correctly named branch (fixed)' (58fed2b, mise 2.0.0).
source: inventory/provenance.md, Added in response to a named real failure (58fed2b)
scope: mise-claude-plugin, one correction on one branch
caveat: One incident, self-reported by the run's own friction log.
